Well, I've been farming these 10.1 mu for 35 years now, and at 55 I know every piece of land like the back of my hand. With just my wife and me at home — our son works in Shijiazhuang at a factory — we've got to be careful with labor, especially during harvest time. I work part-time at a construction site nearby when things are slow on the farm, so we can't be everywhere at once.

Looking at this year, I've got 6 mu in the wheat-maize double crop and 4.1 mu in cotton. Cotton takes a lot of hand-picking labor, but the prices have been decent and it's our cash crop. For the wheat-maize, the turnaround between wheat harvest and maize planting is always tight — sometimes only four or five days — so I need to plan that carefully.

**Wheat (6 mu):** I'll plant in early October, right after the maize comes off. I'm using an improved wheat seed variety — I buy fresh seed every two or three years, and this is the year. I'll put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base before planting, and then at jointing time in spring, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I'll topdress with another 15-20 jin of urea. That's what my neighbor Old Wang does, and he gets good yields. I'll irrigate three times: once after planting if it's dry, once at jointing, and once at flowering. Water costs money — about 20 yuan each time per mu from the well pump — but without it the yield drops badly. I'm expecting around 420 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Summer maize (6 mu, same land):** Right after wheat harvest in early June, I need to get the maize in within a week. I'll use hybrid seed — you can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't work. One bag covers about one mu, costs around 50 yuan. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu, and then maybe topdress with urea at the big-flare stage if it doesn't rain. Two irrigations should be enough if the summer rains are normal. Maize usually gives me about 480 kg per mu.

**Cotton (4.1 mu):** The cotton is already in the ground from April, and I'm finishing picking now in October. For next year's cotton, I'll plant in mid-to-late April again. Cotton needs more pesticide — bollworm is always a problem — so I'll spray three or four times. I'll fertilize with compound fertilizer at planting and add some urea when the plants start flowering. I'll irrigate twice, maybe three times if it's dry. Yield should be around 280 kg per mu of seed cotton. The problem with cotton is the picking — it takes so much labor. With just my wife and me, we'll need to hire people for picking at 100 yuan per day. That's expensive, but we can't pick 4 mu ourselves fast enough.

For labor, my wife and I handle most of the wheat and maize work — planting, fertilizing, spraying. But for cotton picking and the busy harvest/planting windows, I hire 3 or 4 local workers for a few days. Every yuan counts, so I don't buy the most expensive inputs, but I also don't skimp on fertilizer — a bad yield year hurts more than saving a few hundred yuan on urea.
